main:1.text: Jin Sakai meets with Yuna south of Kechi Fishing Village, finding that she had just survived an assassin's attack.  They ride towards a camp that Yuna suspects may have her brother, the blacksmith Taka. They reach the camp and Jin suggests that they go in through the front door and fight honorably. Yuna advises that the prisoners will be killed immediately, so they must take out the Mongols covertly.

main:2.text: Jin sets out to search for Sensei Ishikawa at his dojo to speak with him about the battle at Komoda Beach. Jin introduces himself as Lord Shimura's nephew and asks why the sensei wasn't present at the battle. Sensei Ishikawa claims he was attacked by bandits before he could leave for the battle. Jin and the sensei search for his prodigal archery student, Tomoe.

main:3.text: Jin Sakai goes to the Adachi Estate in search of Masako Adachi. He finds the estate to be empty before being ambushed by guards that were hiding in the guest house. After defeating them, Jin realizes that the men were not Mongols nor were they bandits. He investigates the main house and the stable, then follows a set of footprints and deduces that archers were chasing someone on horseback.

main:4.text: Jin meets up with Yuna in Azamo and finds her in the middle of a discussion with Kenji, a sake brewer and an old friend of hers, and her brother, Taka. Kenji is afraid their plan will not work, but Jin convinces him to help out.

main:5.text: Jin goes to Kishi Grasslands in search of the Straw Hat Ronin. He discovers a burning wagon and a trail of Mongol bodies. He follows the trail, nearly gets ambushed by a Mongol, and runs into his childhood friend, Ryuzo. Jin explains that Lord Shimura is still alive and that he needs all the help he can get to save his uncle.

main:6.text: Yuna and her brother, Taka, have gone to Komatsu Forge ahead of Jin Sakai, but when Jin arrives, he sees Yuna in combat with Mongol soldiers, while Taka and the other villagers have taken refuge inside the forge. When the Mongols have been defeated, Jin asks for Taka's help in creating a tool that can be used to scale the walls of Castle Kaneda.

main:7.text: Jin Sakai and his allies are ready to infiltrate Castle Kaneda and rescue Lord Shimura. After speaking with Yuna, Lady Masako and Sensei Ishikawa, Jin discovers Ryuzo isn't there, but he cannot wait any longer. Jin must become the Ghost again so he doesn't raise any alarms while trying to open the gate for his allies.

main:8.text: Now that Castle Kaneda has been liberated from the Mongols, Jin Sakai, his new allies and Lord Shimura must find a way to defeat Khotun Khan and the entire Mongol army. Their plan involves traveling to Toyotama in an attempt to recruit even more allies to help them fight the invaders.

main:9.text: Jin Sakai must enlist the help of Lord Shimura's pirate contact, Goro, to sail past the Mongol armada and bring a message to the shogunate on the mainland to send additional samurai warriors to combat the Mongol invaders.

main:10.text: Jin Sakai and Yuna must find a way inside Yarikawa Stronghold in an attempt to convince the remaining members of Clan Yarikawa to help join the fight against the Mongol Empire and recapture Castle Shimura. Not only do the people of Yarikawa harbor extreme resentment towards Lord Shimura, but the Mongols have made a huge camp outside the stronghold, making it very difficult for anyone to get inside.

main:11.text: Jin Sakai returns to his family's estate in an attempt to recover his father's armor. As he reunites with Yuriko and Taichi, memories of his youth flood his mind. He visits his father's grave, reminisces with his old caretaker and even learns a few things about his family's past.

main:12.text: With the shogun contacted, the people of Yarikawa recruited, and the clan Sakai armor back in Jin's possession, Jin Sakai and his allies meet up with Lord Shimura at Shimura's camp to discuss a plan of attack towards their goal of reclaiming Castle Shimura.

main:13.text: Lord Shimura has exiled Jin because his ghost techniques do not fit within the bushido code of the samurai. With his horse severely injured, Jin must travel through the frozen landscape of Kamiagata to meet up with Yuna at the Sacred Tree at Kin Sanctuary.

main:15.text: Jin must sneak into his adolescent home, Castle Shimura, and leave a note for his uncle, Lord Shimura, in the hopes that the samurai will join him and his allies in the final battle against Khotun Khan and the Mongol Empire's forces on Tsushima.

side:1.text: Jin goes to Sensei Ishikawa's dojo to pursue Tomoe. Ishikawa had heard of Mongol archers training at the tower near Castle Lookout Hot Spring; the two travel to there and notice a target from afar. Ishikawa tells Jin to go investigate there; and as Jin is doing so, he is ambushed by a few Mongols and their guard dog. He kills them with no help from the sensei, despite him looking from afar.

side:4.text: Dreams of Conquest is the fifth Ishikawa Tale in Ghost of Tsushima. Jin Sakai arrives at a survivor camp to meet with Sensei Ishikawa, who has been searching for his former student Tomoe. He is unable to find Ishikawa and asks a peasant for his whereabouts. The peasant tells Jin that Ishikawa headed out of the camp toward the coast. Heading east, Jin finds Ishikawa pinned down by a group of Mongol archers.

side:5.page: The Ghost and the Demon Sensei
side:5.text: The Ghost and the Demon Sensei is the sixth Ishikawa tale in Ghost of Tsushima.

side:6.text: The Terror of Otsuna is the seventh Ishikawa tale in Ghost of Tsushima. The hunt for Tomoe reaches a breaking point! In The Terror of Otsuna, Jin and Sensei Ishikawa track a new training camp to the rugged Musashi Coast. This mission finally brings Jin face-to-face with Ishikawa's legendary student in a high-speed chase that proves Tomoe is always one step ahead.

side:7.text: Friends in Passing is the eighth Ishikawa Tale during Act 3: Kill the Khan of Ghost of Tsushima.

side:8.text: Laid to Rest is the ninth Ishikawa Tale during Act 3: Kill the Khan of Ghost of Tsushima.

side:9.text: With the list of conspirators in hand, Lady Masako and Jin Sakai are ready to start tracking down the people responsible for the brutal murders of her children and grandchildren. Their first suspect is Sadao, a former member of Clan Adachi and the headman of Kuta Farmstead, appointed by Lady Masako's husband. He fled the farmstead the night of the murders, most likely after hearing of Lady Masako's survival.

side:10.text: Back at the Adachi Estate, Lady Masako is not having any luck speaking with Hina about her husband, Sadao, so Jin Sakai goes inside in an attempt to console Hina by saying that he promises to try to save Sadao's life. Hina offers Jin the information he needs, so he and Lady Masako take a short break outside before hearing Hina screaming from inside the house. They arrive too late and begin to track Hina's killers.

side:11.text: Arriving at the Golden Temple, Jin Sakai must speak with a monk named Junshin about the supply map found on Hachi's body. Junshin tells Jin that he helped set-up the supply camps and gives a copy of the map to the wagon drivers who deliver food to the camps. Jin asks Junshin to spot any location on the map that is not a part of the camp network.

side:13.text: Jin approaches Lady Masako arguing with a monk named Junshin. Masako is tracking down Kajiwara, a former servant of Clan Adachi, for recruiting the men who killed her family. Junshin is aware of Kajiwara's location but is protecting him from Masako for fear for his life. Junshin says Masako is blinded by rage, and Kajiwara is a humble fisherman who would never act against Clan Adachi.

side:17.text: Jin Sakai searches for Lady Masako near Komoda Beach, finds her fighting a group of Mongols and helps her dispatch the remaining enemies. Masako explains that she is searching for the bodies of her two sons so she can give them a proper burial. Jin offers to help and they begin to search the beach.

side:19.text: Jin encounters Kenji waiting by a lamppost. Kenji claims that a nearby Mongol camp is full of resources. Kenji suggests that they should loot the camp now while the Mongols are away from their camp on a raid. Jin agrees to follow Kenji and finds his claim to be true. Jin helps Kenji loot the resources. Kenji mentions not to check one of the yurts, which arouses Jin's suspicion.

side:20.text: Jin meets Kenji near the entrance to Umugi Cove, where he is clearly in distress. Upon being questioned, Kenji reveals that he needs Jin's help again, as he owes a large sum of money to "Gon the Butcher", a dangerous criminal.

side:21.text: After rescuing the warrior monk, Norio, from his imprisonment at Castle Kaneda, Jin Sakai meets up with him at Akashima Village. Norio informs Jin that the Mongols have abducted several monks from the village, including their leader, Hochi, a very skilled healer. Jin and Norio must track down all of the prisoners and bring them back to Akashima.

side:22.text: Although Jin Sakai and Norio were able to rescue some of the monks from the Mongols, there are still several missing, including Hochi. Norio believes he knows where the Mongols are keeping Hochi and asks Jin to help rescue the healer-monk.

side:23.text: Norio is concerned that that Mongols will attack Akashima Village since Hochi has been rescued. Hochi believes they should take shelter at Castle Kaneda as it would be easier to defend, but Jin Sakai believes there's not enough time for everyone to travel there. He and Jin must devise a plan to protect the people by setting up traps using the incense burners that are found throughout the village.

side:24.text: Norio asked Jin Sakai to meet him at Kushi Temple, but as Jin arrived, he found it under attack by the Mongols, as payback for rescuing Hochi. Now, Jin must help Norio and his fellow monks defend the temple from the invaders.

side:25.text: After the Mongol attack on Kushi Temple, Norio discovers the Abbot has gone missing. He and Jin Sakai head out to Koshimizu Farmstead as that is where Norio believes the Abbot may have taken shelter. After further investigation, they realize that the Abbot is not at the farm and end up following a trail of blood to more Mongol enemies. Can Jin and Norio find the Abbot in time?

side:26.text: After promising the monks at Kushi Temple they will recover the lost statue of Buddha, Jin Sakai and Norio head out to investigate. After speaking with a dying monk on the side of the road, they learn the Mongols have a camp to the east. Now all Jin and Norio have to do is defeat the Mongols and find the Buddha.

side:28.text: Jin is supposed to meet Norio in Kamiagata, but comes across a monk “praising” the Mongols, stating if he refuses, they kill not only the monks, but the innocent people as well. He believes Norio will help lead the way to defeat the Mongol threat to Cedar Temple and the monks’ way of life. Jin follows the monk to a farmhouse where Norio is planning to take back Cedar Temple from the enemies.

side:29.text: At Cedar Temple, a monk tells Jin that Norio brought Enjo's ashes to the cemetery at Guardian's Ridge. Norio confides that he found Kharchu's location, but Jin advises that Cedar Temple not only needs his leadership, but revenge is not always the best path for a monk.

side:30.text: On the way to Yarikawa, Yuna hears about the Mongol warlord, Altan, who has been terrorizing the people of Otsuna. He has been stealing food and medicine, and if anyone fights back, they get butchered. Yuna and Jin Sakai seek the help of her childhood friend, Ichi, who runs an inn that is currently inhabited by Mongol soldiers.

side:31.text: Meeting Yuna just outside Mamushi Farmstead, Jin Sakai remarks that the place resembles a small fortress. Yuna offers that it's because the Mamushi brothers don't want anyone knowing what goes on behind their walls: a slave camp where nobody escapes, with the exception of Yuna and Taka. Recalling some terrible memories of her past, Yuna cannot bring herself to enter the farmstead, so Jin offers to go instead.

side:32.text: Yuna confesses to Jin that she had a chance to kill The Black Wolf when she was a child, but couldn't, so now she wants to be the one to kill him. More Mongol soldiers stand in their way, however, but they are no match and Jin and her. When they clear the camp, they realize The Black Wolf isn't there, so they try a Mongol ship that is just off the coast.

side:33.text: Jin Sakai and Yuna head back to Ichi's Inn and speak with an injured Ichi; Altan got their message and said to meet him at a camp near the Kushi-Otsuna border. Ichi is even more bitter now than their first meeting, and still harbors a lot of unspoken resentment towards Yuna, who she calls a dishonorable thief with worthless promises.

side:34.text: Yuriko thinks she remembers the plants to make another type of dart for Jin Sakai's blowgun that are possibly at a nearby cemetery, so she and Jin take a ride towards Kubara Ridge. After defeating the Mongols that set-up camp at the cemetery, Yuriko realizes the plants are not at this cemetery, but probably at another one, belonging to his great-aunt's family, so they mount their horses again.

side:35.text: Seeing that Yuriko is not feeling well, Jin Sakai offers to take her to Akashima, but she asks him for one more indulgence to visit someplace special before she goes to see the healers. They begin their ride through the Serene Forest to an onsen: Maple Shade Hot Spring.

side:36.text: A Healer's Touch is a side tale in Ghost of Tsushima. As Jin approaches a small village near the south seaside, a monk calls for his help. The monk, a healer named Hanaoka, asks Jin for assistance in getting to a camp in the woods, whose residents are ill and in need of a healer. Jin reminds Hanaoka that there are many Mongols and bandits along the way, but assures him that Jin will lead him to the camp.

side:37.text: As Jin is exploring the area west of the Golden Temple in Ariake, a man runs toward him crying for help. Jin asks the man what is wrong, and the man frantically says that the Mongols have taken his house, and his wife and child are there. Jin is disappointed that the man left his family at the house with the Mongols and hurries to the house, which is surrounded by Mongols.

side:38.text: Jin Sakai meets a woman crying outside her house. He asks her what happened, to which she responds that bandits took every last scrap of her food. She tells Jin that they headed northeast, into the woods, and asks Jin to not harm them, to which Jin responds that he can't make any promises.

side:39.text: Jin Sakai meets a Guardian training outside of Azamo Inn. The Guardian tells Jin that she is from Ariake and is searching for the "Azamo League", a group of farmers and fishermen who are fighting back against the Mongols. The Guardian notes that they were supposed to meet her hours ago, and that she was about to go look for them. Jin and the Guardian ride to the farmhouse, where the leaders reside.

side:40.text: After liberating Azamo Bay, Jin Sakai encounters a citizen, Hyoe, that brings Jin his shop to discuss his neighbor, Haruo's clandestine activities at night. Hyoe followed his neighbor to a cemetery and witnessed a meeting with bandits. Jin goes out to the cemetery to investigate and notices a recent fire, some bloody bandages and a half-eaten meal.

side:41.text: Jin Sakai encounters a family at the bridge leading to Hiyoshi Springs, where he is informed by a peasant that his nephew Banta is injured and trapped in the middle of the bridge, which has been surrounded by archers from below whom intend to use the boy as bait to draw the family out onto the bridge, where they will be range of their arrows.

side:42.text: There are worried peasants that alert Jin Sakai to a disturbed man swinging a blade in Kijo Isle, the southernmost point of Izuhara. When Jin arrives, he finds a man named Otosuke practicing with a blade against a dummy. Jin tells Otosuke to stop before he hurts himself; Otosuke stops and confesses that the Mongols took his daughter Maki, and have held her captive in one of the two nearby Mongol EmpirMongol ships.

side:43.text: Jin Sakai approaches a house full of injured survivors. He speaks to one of them, who tells them that there is a merchant working with the Mongols. The Mongols gave the merchant an iron mark, which is what the survivors were trying to take from him. The survivor tells Jin that whoever carries the iron mark is free to travel the roads without fear of being stopped by the Mongols.

side:44.text: Kechi has endured much hardship under the Mongols. I'll take a look around, make sure things are in order.

side:45.text: Jin Sakai approaches a house in Kashine near Shigenori's Peak, and notes how peaceful it is. Civilians are farming and maintaining the property. A female peasant outside the front of the house tells Jin to please go inside, and Lord Jinroku will be back soon. At the back of the house, a female peasant, Nabe, gleefully tells Jin that she gets to prepare Lord Jinroku's bath tonight.

side:46.text: As Jin Sakai approaches the Kii Sake Brewery, he overhears its owner, Kii, asking for a count of the barrels of sake, and notes that the ten they have won't be enough for the Mongols. Jin asks Kii if everything is all right, to which Kii asks if Jin would like a cup of tea. Confused, Jin remarks they are in the famous Kii Sake Brewery of Azamo; Kii asks Jin to follow her to a nearby house.

side:47.text: After freeing Taka from Azamo Bay, Jin Sakai goes back to save the remaining prisoners and emancipate Azamo Bay from the Mongol forces. Jin enters Azamo Bay through a secret opening that he learned about from villagers near the main gate. Jin proceeds to defeat the Mongols, free all of the hostages, including the village elders, and opens all three gates, before searching for the Mongol leader: Harunori.

side:48.text: Jin Sakai meets a man just outside of Yagata Forest, who tells Jin to stay away from the forest, as the spirits of vengeful samurai haunt the place. Jin asks him about the nonsense, to which the man responds that while it used to be place for refuge, now the forest swallows those who enter it, never to be seen again. Jin dismisses this concern, since Tsushima is at war and people go missing all the time.

side:49.text: Jin Sakai encounters a group of dead bandits. The only survivor among them claims that he killed the others. The man, who introduces himself as Gomyo, explains that he was forced into working for the group of bandits in order to pay off his family's debt. However, after the bandits killed his family anyway, Gomyo vowed to hunt down every last one of them. Noting Gomyo's sincerity, Jin agrees to help him.

side:50.text: Jin Sakai encounters a group of Straw Hats attacking Lucky Genzo's Inn. He defeats them all and checks for any survivors of the attack. The only person alive is an old woman. She explains that the ronin attacked the inn and took all of the men to Hollow Gorge. With her dying breath, she begs Jin to save her husband Oda, who was among the men taken.

side:51.text: A woman in Umugi Cove asks Jin Sakai to help her find her daughter Kuma, who disappeared a few days prior. Jin speaks with several people regarding Kuma's whereabouts, including a Straw Hat named Sanetoki who makes cryptic comments comparing children to chickens. Eventually, Jin finds one of Kuma's friends who claims to know where she is.

side:52.page: A Wealthy Man Has All He Needs
side:52.text: Jin Sakai encounters a survivor camp where a merchant is making threats to the survivors. Jin approaches the merchant and asks why he is making threats. The merchant introduces himself as Saburo, and tells Jin that he had planned to escape Tsushima with his family, and paid smugglers to get them past the Mongol naval blockade around the island.

side:53.text: Jin Sakai encounters a man chiseling stone by a broken statue. The man tells Jin to stay away, until he realizes that Jin is not a Mongol. He explains that the broken statue was a work of his father's. Jin recognizes the statue as one of the works of Master Izo, a master sculptor; and that the man in front of him is Master Izo's son. The man tells Jin that Mongols defaced the statue and killed his father.

side:55.text: The Burden of Theft is a tale of Tsushima that becomes available during Act 2: Retake Castle Shimura.

side:56.text: The Generosity of Lady Sanjo is a tale of Tsushima that becomes available during Act 2: Retake Castle Shimura. Lady Sanjo invites Jin Sakai to join her for some tea, though admits that she only did so out of politeness. Having heard of his capabilities from Kenji, she asks Jin for his help in retrieving a map containing the location of food stores.

side:57.text: Jin Sakai encounters a distraught woman named Shino who claims her father was abducted by a kappa. Suspecting that man rather than demon was responsible, Jin searches the area and finds a set of tracks leading across the river. There, he finds the dead body of Shino's father. He follows more tracks and is led to a bandit camp.

side:59.text: Fit for the Khan is a side tale that becomes available in Act 3: Kill the Khan as soon as Honor and Ash is completed. A Blacksmith Apprentice requests Jin's help to retrieve an armor set that his master was forced to create for Khotun Khan (Even if the Khan is dead, the Mongols still want the armor as a prize).

side:60.text: Hidden in Snow is a side tale in Ghost of Tsushima. Jin Sakai arrives in Sago Mill. The town is deserted save for a few men who all greet Jin nervously. Sota, the person in charge, explains that he and his people are wary of strangers because of encounters with Mongols and bandits. Jin offers his help but Sota declines, saying that their real problems—disease and starvation—cannot be solved with a blade.

side:61.text: The Cost of Fear is a tale of Tsushima that becomes available during Act 3: Kill the Khan. Jin Sakai encounters a man dying on the side of the road. He tells Jin that he has been poisoned along with the rest of his family, who retreated back to their home.
